solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One in a well, keen to pull themselves up?

definitions.note: an adjective for people who are keen to rise; the question mark marks the playful phrasing

indicators.note: in tells us the word for one sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a spring is a natural well of water
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at the bottom of a well, eager to haul themselves out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside A SPRING. The definition reads literally in the surface but means ambitious.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring people are ambitious, wanting to raise their status or better their position.

clue.text: Old beset by criticism, mostly long-suffering

indicators.note: something beset by another thing is surrounded by it, so the abbreviation for old goes inside
mostly means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'

explanation.surface: An elderly person who has endured years of criticism with patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims STICK to STIC; 'beset by' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without complaint, which is what long-suffering describes.

clue.text: Urgently request ancient stories of devils?

indicators.note: lore of devils is written devil-lore, so the word for devils comes first

parts.note: an imp is a small devil
lore is a body of traditional stories and beliefs

explanation.surface: A curious reader asking, rather insistently, for old tales about demons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' reverses the clue order: lore of imps becomes IMP + LORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg someone earnestly, a stronger word for asking.

clue.text: Freeze ingredient for milk pudding that's not started

indicators.note: not started says the first letter of the ingredient is missing

parts.note: rice pudding is a classic milk pudding, so rice is its ingredient

explanation.surface: A recipe step: chill an ingredient for a dessert that has not yet been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not started' drops the R from RICE. Rice pudding is a traditional British dessert of rice baked in milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice something is to freeze it or chill it with frozen water.

clue.text: Good and moving death for mafia chief

indicators.note: moving means these letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mobster arranging a fine, poignant death for a mafia boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like 'touching' but is the anagram signal for the two words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Godfather is the head of a mafia family, made famous by the Puzo novel and film.

clue.text: Cricketers take them out to lunch

definitions.meaning: cricketers carry ... out to the crease
slang for crazy, which is also what ... means

explanation.surface: Cricket players take something out to the lunch interval of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket stops for lunch, so 'out to lunch' seems to continue the cricket scene, but it is a slang phrase for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is the bat used in cricket in the plural, and also British slang for crazy, like out to lunch.

clue.text: Herb, one about to be cut from church building

indicators.note: cut from means the following letters are removed from the church word

parts.note: a basilica is a large church building
the Roman numeral for one is I
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A herb grown next to a church building, part of which is about to be pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut from' removes I and CA from the end of BASILICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a fragrant culinary herb used widely in Italian cooking.

clue.text: One needs time and motivation for such a crime

parts.note: a reason is a motive for acting

explanation.surface: A detective's maxim: a criminal needs opportunity and motive to commit this offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One needs' and 'for' are linking words; the clue echoes the detective's mantra of means and motive.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Body of rook found in small wood

indicators.note: found in says the chess abbreviation is placed inside the wood

parts.note: a copse is a small group of trees
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook's dead body discovered in a little wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts R inside COPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a corpse is the dead body of a person, so 'Body' in the crime-story sense fits.

clue.text: I'd reversed some magic said to make disappear

indicators.note: reversed says the letters of I'd are read backwards

parts.note: taken as its letters, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: said tells us the magic word is heard, not seen, and spelt to fit

parts.note: a spell is a piece of magic

explanation.surface: A magician uses a reversed incantation to make something vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns ID into DI; 'said' gives SPELL as heard, entered as SPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or banish, so doubts or fears are made to vanish.

clue.text: City house is sound again

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A city house is in good condition once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'in good repair' but is the verb, to resound. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat a noise, as when it bounces back off a wall.

clue.text: Perfect female breaking all the rules

parts.note: lawless describes someone who ignores every rule

explanation.surface: A woman who seems ideal yet flouts every rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless has no faults, which makes it perfect.

clue.text: Secret society member criminal men so fear

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted and rearranged

explanation.surface: Criminals are scared of the members of a hidden fraternity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges MEN SO FEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons belong to a fraternal order famous for its secret rituals.

clue.text: Waterbird heads for good river estuary to live

indicators.note: heads for means the opening letters of the next three words are taken

parts.note: to be is to exist, or live

explanation.surface: A waterbird making for a pleasant estuary where it can settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads for' looks like 'travels towards' but takes G, R, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving bird of lakes and rivers.

clue.text: English law set up after weapon used in part of boat

indicators.note: after places the reversed part behind the weapon word

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so reversed

explanation.surface: An English law was drawn up after a weapon was fired on a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' suits a down clue, where reversing reads upwards; the result is WALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side.

clue.text: Smell article relating to a person

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news story about someone's body odour.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a hum is an unpleasant smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Human is the adjective for things belonging to people.

clue.text: Joke grasped by May Queen?

indicators.note: grasped by says the joke is held inside the month

parts.note: a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A May Queen gets a joke at the village fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May Queen' is a single phrase in the surface, a girl crowned at May Day festivities, but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is the title of a monarch, as in Her Majesty, so it can stand for a queen; the question mark flags the indirectness.

clue.text: Grass covered by mould?

definitions.meaning: grass is slang for someone who tells tales to the police
whimsically, one who is in a form or mould

explanation.surface: A lawn overrun with fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for a police informant. The second reading splits the answer as IN FORM-ER, someone in a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer tells on people to the police, which is what a grass does.

clue.text: Beginning working group

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A newly formed team getting down to work.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its start.

clue.text: Moral project involving saint

indicators.note: involving means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: to project is to jut out

explanation.surface: An ethical scheme with a saint taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun but is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: Just describes behaviour that is fair and right.

clue.text: Small company about to be successful

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A small firm on the brink of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be' reads as 'on the verge of', but 'about' is RE and 'to be successful' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to succeed, as in scoring a hit or a goal.

clue.text: State offering some Alaskans a subsidy

indicators.note: offering some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A government gives Alaskans some financial support.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Part of school programme's more taken off?

definitions.meaning: one class in a school timetable
if more clothing is taken off

explanation.surface: A school programme in which more is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into LESS ON, what is left when more is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons are the classes that make up a school timetable.

clue.text: Owl flying close to the ground

indicators.note: flying sends the bird's letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An owl swooping just above the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges OWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Low means not high, near ground level.

clue.text: Thaw encountered around heart of Himalayas

indicators.note: around says the meeting word wraps round the middle letter

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: heart of picks the central letter of the mountain range's name

explanation.surface: A thaw meeting climbers in the middle of the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes L, the centre of HIMALAYAS; 'around' puts MET round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt is to thaw, turning ice into water.

clue.text: Modern left party's ending — we had a new union member

parts.note: new means modern

indicators.note: ending says only the final letter of party is used

parts.note: we'd is short for we had

explanation.surface: A left-wing party newcomer joins as a trade union member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes Y from party. The 'union' is a marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A newlywed has just joined a marriage, a union of two people.
